note: Pinned-Letta no-compaction + request-time capacity protection. The patch applies on top of the reviewed multicall patch (ae-multicall-receive-compat-1) and the SERVICE now loads that stacked tree under its own declared profile (see stack-manifest.json and `ae_multicall.STACK_ENV_VAR`); the order of the patch chain is part of the contract. Nothing here changes the upstream default: an agent with no AE capacity tag compacts exactly as before.

verification.note: offline_patch_verified means the stacked bytes equal the pinned baseline plus the reviewed multicall patch plus this reviewed patch plus this round's staged helper sources. applied_to_live_server is only set once the running service itself produced a stack load receipt; the audit requires that receipt and never accepts a client-built one.

policy.name: ae-no-compaction
policy.declared_by: the AE driver's agent creation payload tags, one per agent
enforced_at: letta/services/summarizer/compact.py::compact_messages - the single place a compaction reaches a summariser, reached from BOTH pinned trigger paths (post_step_context_check and context_window_exceeded)
letta/agents/letta_agent_v3.py::LettaAgentV3.step - the request-time capacity gate, immediately after the final provider request is built
policy.unknown_policy: refused: an unrecognised ae-no-compaction:* tag raises instead of falling back to the upstream default
policy.default_behaviour: unchanged: no tag means no guard and no gate

patch.adds: nothing: the two helper modules are NOT in the patch, because the checkout is rebuilt by copying the staged sources and their digests are checked separately

letta/helpers/ae_no_compaction.py.provides: policy_state / require_no_compaction / no_compaction_declared (the summariser guard), `capacity_gate_decision` (the request-time decision, refusing a missing or undeclared counting basis) and `dict_request_contract` (the pinned wire-request contract check)

letta/helpers/ae_qwen_tokenizer.py.note: generated from ae_multiturn_capacity.py by tools/stage_letta_tokenizer.py; tools/check_tokenizer_drift.py proves the two stay identical. It carries the SAME `count_request_prompt` entry the report and the proxy use, so the service gate and the capacity report count one contract, not two.

letta/agents/letta_agent_v3.py.baseline_is: the multicall-patched bytes of the pinned checkout

letta/services/summarizer/compact.py.baseline_is: the multicall-patched bytes of the pinned checkout

count_basis: official_qwen_tokenizer: the shared `count_request_prompt` entry over the exact request body (messages incl. the system prompt, and the wire tool schemas), rendered with the official chat template and tokenized with the official assets

pinned_token_counter: Letta's own `count_tokens_with_tools`; consulted ONLY after a primary count exists and used only when it counts MORE, so the gate can only get stricter and an approximation can never authorise
capacity_gate.no_fallback: a byte length or bytes-per-token ratio can UNDER-estimate (10000 ASCII digits are 10000 official tokens but ~4167 at 2.4 bytes/token), so a request whose primary count is missing or raises is REFUSED rather than passed or approximated
capacity_gate.count_source_required: the decision record must name the counting basis it used; an empty or missing `count_source` is refused as `count_source_undeclared`
capacity_gate.asset_identity: the counting assets must be the ones the run declared (`capacity.tokenizer`); a family or exploration asset is labelled as such, and the RUN-stage decision refuses an exploration asset
capacity_gate.boundary: input + THIS role's own output reserve <= the declared context_window
capacity_gate.claim: offline compatibility evidence only; the live-load claim needs the service's own stack load receipt (see stack-manifest.json)

patch_base: the reviewed multicall-patched checkout (deployment-assets/letta-multicall/ae-multicall-letta.patch applied to the pinned upstream checkout)

deployment_layout.service_checkout: the STACKED checkout (multicall + this patch): the service loads it under AE_LETTA_PATCH_STACK_PROFILE=ae-no-compaction-stack-1, whose manifest (deployment-assets/letta-no-compaction/stack-manifest.json) pins every changed and new file
deployment_layout.multicall_only_checkout: kept for the earlier multicall protocol: its manifest, checkout and load receipt are unchanged, so a protocol that never declared the capacity contract keeps its identity
deployment_layout.receipt: the service process writes a stack load receipt after resolving the files it really imports; a client-built receipt is never accepted
deployment_layout.why: the r2 layout ran the service from the multicall-only checkout and the agents from a separate stacked tree; R3-1 closed that gap by giving the stacked tree its own declared profile, manifest and receipt instead of a second tree
